parts:
Working through my brand new (10 day old) copy (from Amazon) of the old (2009) book. I was doing pretty well until I hit Chapter 5, specifically 5.8 and 5.9. (With some help from this list I seem to be back on track for 5.10). 

I have a series of what strike me as very basic questions. After having spent serious hours searching the web and downloading other documentation (including the 12.12.05 version of the "Package 'ggplot2'" documentation), reading, re-reading, and typing the code in several times (in case there was something in my code that I was blind to) I still have my questions, . . .  so in the hopes that some fellow survivor of the Mayan apocalypse will pause from rebuilding society long enough to post a few answers . . . here are a few very simple, very basic questions:  

#1 -- Is there code for figures 5.14, 5.15, 5.16, and 5.17??? 

#2 -- On page 84 what the heck does "m2" refer to??? (I found a pdf of the book on the web and was able to do a search on "m2" electronically - "m2" is found on page 84 and as part of an address in two other places.) Please note that before bombarding this list with queries I also downloaded the 12.12.05 version of the "Package 'ggplot2'"" documentation. There is an "m2" there as well but it must refer to a different dataframe as the results I get are very different than the pix on p.84. 

#3 -- I seem to have lost the referent for "m" (last line on p84)  as I can't reproduce the fig at the top of p85 either. (I assume that "m" is the car database, but when I apply the "iqr" function and then the "m + stat_summary(fun.data = "iqr", geom="ribbon")" I get a plot with "hwy" on the ordinate and "cyl" on the abscissa!!

Many thanks!

Wayne

ggplot(d, aes(x=lcarat, y=lprice, colour=color)) + geom_point()

ggplot(d, aes(x=lcarat, y=lprice2, colour=color)) + geom_point()

ggplot(color, aes(x=color, y=fit, ymin=lower, ymax=upper)) +

messages.author: d5592d7486b845bb
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 - THE BOOK - help needed by a fellow Mayan Apocalypse survivor!!!
parts:
Hi,

I stumbled upon this while searching for the functions for these plots by myself.

Here they are:

# Fig 5.17
data(movies)
ggplot(movies, aes(x=year, y=rating)) + geom_blank() +
  stat_summary(fun.y = "median", geom = "line")

ggplot(movies, aes(x=year, y=rating)) + geom_blank() +
  stat_summary(fun.data=median_hilow, geom = "smooth")

ggplot(movies, aes(x=year, y=rating)) + geom_blank() +
  stat_summary(fun.y = "mean", geom = "line")

ggplot(movies, aes(x=year, y=rating)) + geom_blank() +
  stat_summary(fun.data=mean_cl_boot, geom = "smooth")

ggplot(movies, aes(x=round(rating), y=log10(votes))) + geom_blank() +
  stat_summary(fun.y = "mean", geom = "point")

ggplot(movies, aes(x=round(rating), y=log10(votes))) + geom_blank() +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_cl_normal, geom = "errorbar")

ggplot(movies, aes(x=round(rating), y=log10(votes))) + geom_blank() +
  stat_summary(fun.data = median_hilow, geom = "pointrange")

ggplot(movies, aes(x=round(rating), y=log10(votes))) + geom_blank() +
  stat_summary(fun.data = median_hilow, geom = "crossbar")

# Chapter 5.9.1
m2 <- ggplot(movies, aes(x= round(rating), y=log10(votes))) + geom_blank()
midm <- function(x) mean(x, trim=0.5)
m2 + stat_summary(aes(colour="trimmed"),fun.y=midm, geom="point") +
  stat_summary(aes(colour="raw"),fun.y=mean, geom="point") +
  scale_color_hue("mean")

# Chapter 5.9.2
m <- ggplot(movies, aes(x=year, y=rating)) + geom_blank()
iqr <- function(x,...) {
  qs <- quantile(as.numeric(x), c(0.25,0.75), na.rm=T)
  names(qs) <- c("ymin", "ymax")
  qs
}
m + stat_summary(fun.data="iqr", geom="ribbon")
# End

Have fun!
Hans
